text:
vivian: quick check-in: default pattern for private/VPC customers regional peers vs single-account egress bridge? need default + fallback story.

alex: regional peers = lower p99, fewer hops. cons: per-region routing state, ENI limits, more IPs.

mike: egress bridge = single audit point, easier KMS/flow-logs, predictable IP pool. cons: extra hop adds ~10ms, need NAT/scale plumbing.

kristin: control-plane: peers are simple (attach + advertise). bridge needs lifecycle APIs + health checks + attach semantics.

vivian: what about automatic fallback if a peer dies?

alex: doable: keep a lower-priority route pointing to bridge. if peering withdraws, traffic hits bridge. need dampening to avoid oscillation.

mike: SNAT differences matter. if customers expect stable egress IP, bridge flip will break them. solution: shared static egress pools that both paths can use, or sidecar SNAT on bridge.

kristin: recommend: default to regional peers for small/medium tenants, bridge as fallback and recommendation for very large tenants to avoid ENI explosion.

vivian: billing? meter per-GB-per-region or hide in infra fee?

alex: meter per-GB for transparency. finance will ask for aggregation windows to reduce invoice churn.

mike: action items: prototype SNAT shim (mike), define ENI thresholds (alex), add dashboards/alerts (infra-bot).

infra-bot: noted: will add dashboard request for peering health, ENI usage, gateway nat-conns.

vivian: summary: regional peers default, bridge fallback via lower-priority route, static egress pool for IP stability, per-GB billing with aggregation. we'll capture in RFC follow-up. :thumbsup:
